conditioning.name: Field introduction - Sat 3 Oct 2026
conditioning.purpose: Introduce rugby acceleration and movement quality.

warmUp.name: Brisk walk
warmUp.detail: 200 m brisk walking.

warmUp.name: Easy jog
warmUp.detail: 200 m easy straight-line jogging; walk any turns.

warmUp.name: Marching knee lifts
warmUp.detail: 20 m alternating marching knee lifts, small controlled steps.

warmUp.name: Heel-to-toe walk

warmUp.name: Side steps
warmUp.detail: 20 m leading left, then 20 m leading right; feet do not cross.

Walking distance is the minimum recovery; wait longer if breathing or legs are not ready. Stop if speed or control fades.

main.name: Walking shuttle pattern
main.detail: 4 x (10 m walk out + 10 m walk back). Total 80 m. Turn using several small steps in a broad arc; alternate turn direction. This is pattern practice, not sprinting.
roundDetails: 10 m walk out + 10 m walk back

conditioning.howToUse: Complete prescribed metres, not minutes. startMin/endMin are approximate scheduling windows, including ample recovery and cone setup. trainingPlans.name: Loosehead Comeback - Conditioning - Sep 2026 to Jan 2027
trainingPlans.source: Rewritten with ChatGPT, 27 September 2026; revised with Claude, 27 September 2026. Phase 1: Monday/Wednesday/Friday evening treadmill and optional short Saturday morning field practice. Phase 2: Tuesday evening floodlit field, Thursday evening treadmill maintenance, Saturday morning daylight field. Thursday field moved to Saturday because the Thursday lane is unlit. Field prescriptions, warm-ups, slow-downs, recoveries and cooldowns are in metres. Minute windows estimate scheduling only. Treadmill flow: floor mobility first, warm-up walk at start of main, uninterrupted treadmill work through walking cool-down.

goal.primaryGoal: Build a continuous 5 km aerobic base while introducing low-volume acceleration, then increase emphasis on solo rugby field conditioning alongside five weekday morning strength sessions.
goal.baseline: 4 x 5 minutes at 7 km/h, with 2 minutes walking between repetitions.

checkpoints.target: Around 30 minutes continuous at an easy pace if progression is comfortable.
First continuous 5000 m, distance led. At 7 km/h expect about 42 min 51 sec; no 30-minute requirement.
Maintain easy 5 km capacity and tolerate controlled short accelerations, shuttles and repeat efforts; review separate contact readiness.

goal.weeklySchedule: 28 September-8 November: Monday/Wednesday/Friday evenings treadmill, Saturday mornings short field technique; listed exceptions apply. First 5 km on Saturday 7 November replaces field, with Friday 6 November off. From 9 November: Tuesday evening floodlit field (Field A), Thursday evening treadmill maintenance, Saturday morning daylight field (Field B).
goal.importInstructions: Replace the previous conditioning plan using the unchanged planName. All sessions are explicitly dated in existingRunPlan; no recurring items or overrides. Keep the separate strength plan. Actual importer not tested.
goal.progressionGate: Only advance when conversational running, normal gait and next-day knee/shin response are comfortable. Repeat or shorten if needed. New swelling, locking, giving way or increasing pain means stop the provoking activity and seek assessment. Dates are provisional, not deadlines.
goal.fieldEntry: Early field work is submaximal technique, not sprint testing. Progress only with symptom-free running, comfortable leg training and good next-day recovery. After the MCL injury, seek a sports-physio return-to-sport check before faster accelerations and direction changes if readiness has not been assessed. No maximal sprinting in this plan.
goal.ifMilestoneDelayed: If 5 km is not comfortable by 7 November, retain the last successful treadmill stage on the existing Monday/Wednesday/Friday slots instead of starting the Tuesday/Thursday/Saturday block. Keep Saturday field optional or omit. Do not run both schedules. Apply the same travel/rest dates; start the first field phase when ready, never jump to a later workload.
goal.equipment: Treadmill; field timer for reference only, cones or marker bottles, measured 40 m lane plus 10 m runoff, reliable grip and lighting (Tuesday floodlights, Saturday daylight). Walk return trips to accumulate specified recovery metres.
goal.pace: Treadmill: 7 km/h starting reference, 0% incline; 6.5 km/h or slower if required for conversation. Walking recovery 4.5 km/h. Field: distance-led with perceived-speed ceilings, not stopwatch races. Acceleration walk recovery is a minimum; wait longer when needed.
goal.combinedLoad: Initial pattern is up to nine sessions across six days: five morning gym sessions, three evening treadmill sessions and one optional short field session. This is a ceiling, not a completion quota. Friday/Saturday are consecutive impact exposures, so Friday is shorter and Saturday technique is optional. Drop Saturday first if recovery is incomplete. Sunday remains rest. After 9 November, conditioning returns to three sessions weekly.
goal.buffer: All minute windows remain for importer compatibility. Field completion is determined by metres, not time; do not add repetitions to fill the booking. Time allocations include recovery, setup and transitions. Treadmill main work is time/speed led except continuous distance targets.

exceptions.reason: London travel: 5 October evening departure, 7 October away. Resume Friday 9 October.
Wedding; 31 October field is optional only if recovered.
Conditioning rest before first 5 km on Saturday 7 November.
Low Wood Bay trip; no Saturday field session. Thursday 3 December treadmill is that week's run.

goal.30Minute5K: A 30-minute 5 km requires 10 km/h. Current baseline is 4 x 5 minutes at 7 km/h. Establish continuous distance first; this block does not promise a 30-minute result. Consider a later speed-focused running block once 5 km and rugby conditioning are consistently comfortable.
goal.strengthInteraction: Monday evening treadmill follows lower-body strength: stay easy, reduce if legs are heavy. Wednesday power work remains optional if the added running creates soreness. From 9 November the gym swaps Thursday to upper body and Friday to lower body, so the Thursday 5 km follows fresh legs and Saturday Field B follows Friday legs at easy effort. Conditioning does not justify adding extra gym work.
goal.treadmillFlow: Floor mobility first, then one continuous treadmill visit: main begins with the five-minute warm-up walk, followed by running/recovery blocks and the walking cool-down. Final stretches follow after dismounting. All setup buffer is before boarding. Running distance targets exclude walking.

readinessRules: Field distances govern completion; minute windows are only estimates. Never rush recovery to meet the timer.
Initial Saturday field is optional because it follows Friday running. Skip with heavy legs, soreness, poor sleep or adverse knee/shin response.
No maximal sprinting, sharp pivoting or contact drills. Short controlled efforts are preparation for later rugby demands.
Stop provoking work for swelling, increasing pain, locking or giving way; seek assessment.

Use a flat, well-lit, non-slippery field lane with runoff: floodlights on Tuesday, daylight on Saturday. Never run field work in the dark. If unavailable, skip field or replace with easy treadmill work, not extra sessions.
Skip field work on frost, ice or standing water; replace with easy treadmill work.
Keep Saturday Field B easy after Friday lower-body lifting. Wednesday gym power work can be omitted when running fatigue accumulates.
Solo conditioning does not establish readiness for scrummaging, tackling or match play; arrange graded coached contact separately.
If team training begins it replaces, rather than adds to, a corresponding field session. No missed-session catch-up.
